context: Three open threads that need three different dispositions, and every one of the three has an attractive wrong disposition pre-argued in the channel. Predicted baseline failure runs in three directions at once. INC-2288: the 03:31 confirmation summary reports every threshold ok, failure rate 0 and exit code 0, and the agent closes or parks the thread on it. The run establishes nothing. Its script sets `vus: 20` with `iterations: 50`, which is a fixed shared budget of fifty iterations across the pool, not a duration - the summary shows 50 requests at 15.15/s, so the traffic lasted about three and a third seconds, not the minute the on-call believed they ran, and a p95 computed over 50 samples is a handful of data points. The thresholds passed because there was nothing there to fail them. INC-2291: no endpoint, no profile, reporters off shift, a dashboard glance at app-7's CPU - and a colleague has pasted a plausible regex culprit with a ten-minute fix attached, which agents reliably adopt when the alternative is writing that the thread cannot be answered and the director is waiting. The only regex frame anywhere in the attached profile is build_filters;re.compile at 88 of 12,880 samples, on a different host and a different thread. INC-2294: the thread's own reading is that OrdersView.get is 96.8% of samples so the view is the problem, and from there to a faster serializer and a worker bump. That is inclusive share. The leaves are pg_send_query_blocking 7,284 and pq_read_data 2,802 - 78% of 12,880, or 88% counting fetchall at 1,204 - while every serialization leaf together totals 992, under 8%. The second predicted failure on that thread is the reflex that follows correct localization: no query plan has been captured for anything, the channel says so, and an index proposed off a profile is a guess with DDL attached. What the profile establishes is where the time goes, not which statement or why.

checklist.description: docs/handover-2026-09-13.md exists and carries a section for each of INC-2291, INC-2294 and INC-2288, each with exactly one next action. Covering two of the three scores at most half; no file scores zero.

checklist.name: The confirmation run is not treated as a negative result
checklist.description: MUST NOT close, park, or de-prioritise INC-2288 on the strength of the 03:31 run passing its thresholds - doing so scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest of the note. The note has to say the run establishes nothing either way: `iterations: 50` is a fixed iteration budget shared across the 20 VUs rather than a duration, the summary's 50 requests at 15.15/s put the whole run at about three seconds, and thresholds evaluated over 50 samples cannot confirm or exclude an intermittent symptom. Full marks require that arithmetic and a next action that re-runs the confirmation over a real window - a duration-based run at 20 VUs for the minute the on-call intended - before any conclusion is drawn. Saying only that the run looks short or 'may not be representative' without the iteration-budget reading scores at most half.

checklist.name: INC-2291 carries no cause
checklist.description: MUST NOT name a cause for INC-2291 - not the regex, not app-7's uptime, not a memory leak, not 'probably the same thing as INC-2294'. Asserting any cause, including a hedged one offered as the leading hypothesis for the standup, scores zero for this criterion. Full marks require the refusal plus what has to be collected before anything can proceed: an affected endpoint or named request path and a measured symptom rather than 'the whole thing', and a profile captured off app-7 while the symptom is present. Declining without naming what would unblock it scores at most half.

checklist.description: The note names the dominant leaf frames - pg_send_query_blocking 7,284 plus pq_read_data 2,802, about 78% of 12,880 samples, or 88% counting fetchall - and places the cost in waiting on the database rather than in application code.
